objects.statement: Persistent point-in-time improvement in technology cost per unit of performance is associated with a higher probability of broad economic deployment than a flat or worsening cost curve.
objects.null_hypothesis: Cost/performance improvement has no incremental relationship with later deployment after conditioning on technology family and time.
objects.eligible_universe: technology families with consistent cost and performance definitions
objects.conditioning_state: technology family, release cohort, macro funding regime
objects.falsification_rule: Fail if walk-forward tests do not beat a flat-cost baseline or if sign stability disappears across held-out technology families.

objects.statement: Positive acceleration in penetration or active adoption precedes broad diffusion more often than level-only adoption measures.
objects.null_hypothesis: Adoption acceleration adds no out-of-sample information beyond current adoption level.
objects.target_variable: future penetration / transition into broad diffusion
objects.eligible_universe: products or technologies with PIT active-adopter and eligible-population series
objects.conditioning_state: current penetration level and cohort age
objects.falsification_rule: Fail if acceleration does not improve held-out forecasting or produces unstable signals under plausible denominator revisions.

objects.statement: Positive velocity and acceleration of point-in-time narrative mentions across independent sources predicts continued near-term diffusion better than narrative popularity level alone.
objects.null_hypothesis: Mention velocity and acceleration add no incremental information beyond current mention level.
objects.eligible_universe: narratives with timestamped source-level text observations
objects.conditioning_state: current attention level, source base and market regime
objects.falsification_rule: Fail if walk-forward Brier/log-loss or turning-point metrics do not improve versus level-only baselines after source deduplication.

objects.statement: High source saturation combined with accelerating counter-narrative prevalence predicts weaker marginal diffusion or reversal risk.
objects.null_hypothesis: Saturation and counter-narrative growth do not predict a reduction in subsequent narrative diffusion.
objects.target_variable: future marginal mention growth / transition to decay
objects.eligible_universe: narratives with source diversity and counter-narrative labels
objects.conditioning_state: attention level, prior velocity, source saturation
objects.falsification_rule: Fail if high-saturation observations do not show lower future marginal diffusion than matched non-saturated observations across regime holdouts.

objects.statement: Sustained acceleration in company revenue share relative to its industry is associated with higher probability of future right-tail value creation.
objects.null_hypothesis: Market-share acceleration has no incremental relation to future right-tail outcomes after controlling for size and industry growth.
objects.target_variable: future top-decile wealth creation / sustained value-capture outperformance
objects.eligible_universe: companies with PIT company and industry revenue series
objects.conditioning_state: size, industry growth, starting share, capital intensity
objects.falsification_rule: Fail if cross-sectional held-out top-tail precision and wealth-tail recall do not exceed level-only and size baselines.

objects.statement: Persistent demand-to-supply tightness at a controlled bottleneck is associated with disproportionate value capture by the bottleneck owner or controller.
objects.null_hypothesis: Measured bottleneck scarcity does not improve future value-capture outcomes beyond industry growth and current profitability.
objects.target_variable: future value capture / pricing power / share concentration
objects.eligible_universe: industries with measurable capacity, demand and identifiable bottleneck control
objects.conditioning_state: capacity cycle, substitution risk, customer concentration
objects.falsification_rule: Fail if scarcity pressure is not followed by higher value capture or if substitution erodes the effect in held-out cases.

objects.statement: State-conditioned extreme-tail models improve calibration and event discrimination versus unconditional tail-frequency baselines.
objects.null_hypothesis: Conditioning on current state variables provides no improvement in extreme-event probability forecasts.
objects.target_variable: probability of predefined extreme return/drawdown event
objects.eligible_universe: liquid assets with sufficient PIT return and state histories
objects.conditioning_state: volatility, drawdown and approved PIT state variables
objects.falsification_rule: Fail if walk-forward calibration, PR-AUC or false-alarm tradeoffs do not beat unconditional POT and simple volatility-threshold baselines.

objects.statement: A regime-switching model can identify a statistically distinct extreme-risk regime with better out-of-sample calibration than fixed rolling-volatility thresholds.
objects.null_hypothesis: Latent-regime models add no stable information beyond rolling volatility and drawdown thresholds.
objects.target_variable: extreme-regime membership and next-horizon tail risk
objects.eligible_universe: liquid assets with long PIT return histories
objects.falsification_rule: Fail if regime labels are unstable, not reproducible, or provide no held-out calibration/lead-time improvement after complexity penalty.

objects.statement: Exposure structures with explicitly bounded downside and open upside can improve realized right-tail capture relative to left-tail damage net of premium and transaction costs versus linear exposure.
objects.null_hypothesis: Convex payoff structures provide no net improvement in right-tail capture to left-tail damage after costs.
objects.target_variable: realized payoff asymmetry net of costs
objects.eligible_universe: instruments with observable prices, contract terms and liquidity
objects.conditioning_state: underlying price, implied volatility, horizon, transaction costs
objects.falsification_rule: Fail if net realized asymmetry does not exceed matched linear exposure or if modelled downside bounds are routinely violated by liquidity/implementation effects.

objects.statement: Reverse-DCF implied growth and margin assumptions provide more informative valuation context for future expectation gaps than simple valuation-multiple percentiles.
objects.null_hypothesis: Reverse-DCF implied expectations add no held-out information beyond simple multiple percentiles.
objects.target_variable: future expectation revision / valuation realization gap
objects.eligible_universe: companies with PIT enterprise value, revenue, margins and free cash flow
objects.conditioning_state: sector economics, capital intensity, starting profitability
objects.falsification_rule: Fail if implied-expectation states do not improve held-out discrimination or are dominated by plausible discount-rate sensitivity.

objects.statement: Explicit ruin, expected-shortfall, drawdown and liquidity constraints reduce non-survivable portfolio outcomes relative to an unconstrained return-maximizing baseline while preserving a material share of geometric growth.
objects.null_hypothesis: Survival constraints do not reduce ruin-like outcomes or destroy geometric growth enough to negate their benefit.
objects.target_variable: ruin/breach frequency and geometric wealth growth
objects.eligible_universe: self-financing portfolios with PIT positions and returns
objects.falsification_rule: Fail if constrained policies do not materially reduce breach/ruin outcomes or if geometric growth is consistently inferior to simpler conservative baselines.

objects.statement: Fractional Kelly sizing with explicit uncertainty shrinkage improves the geometric-growth/survival tradeoff relative to full Kelly and fixed-size baselines under estimation error.
objects.null_hypothesis: Fractional/robust Kelly provides no stable improvement over full Kelly or fixed-size baselines under held-out uncertainty.
objects.target_variable: geometric growth subject to ruin/drawdown constraints
objects.eligible_universe: strategies with PIT probability/payoff estimates and realized outcomes
objects.conditioning_state: estimation uncertainty, tail risk, liquidity and correlation
objects.falsification_rule: Fail if robust fractional sizing does not reduce overbetting damage or does not improve constrained geometric growth across regime holdouts.
